from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: From Discrete to Continuous", 
                          ["Discrete probability uses bars for distinct outcomes.", 
                           "Continuous variables mean zero probability at exact points.", 
                           "Focus shifts from bar height to area under curves."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show text 'Discrete Probability' at left in #FF5733.
        discrete_text = Text("Discrete Probability", color="#FF5733", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(discrete_text, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(discrete_text), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        
        bar_chart = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=0.5 + i*0.2, width=0.4, color=WHITE).set_fill(WHITE, opacity=0.8) for i in range(4)])
        bar_chart.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1, aligned_edge=DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(bar_chart, 'C2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(bar_chart))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show text 'Continuous Probability' at right in #33FF57.
        continuous_text = Text("Continuous Probability", color="#33FF57", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(continuous_text, 'B5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(continuous_text), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the PDF", [
            "PDF defines probability through area under a curve.",
            "Two rules: curve is positive and area is one.",
            "Total area represents hundred percent certainty."
        ])
        
        # Axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 2, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # PDF curve (f(x))
        func = lambda x: 0.5 * x * np.exp(-0.5 * x) * 4 # Simplified PDF shape
        curve = axes.plot(func, color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(axes), Create(curve))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#33A1FF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        ineq = MathTex("f(x) \geq 0", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(ineq, "A3")
        self.play(Write(ineq))
        
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, 4], color="#33A1FF", opacity=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(area))
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        total_prob = MathTex(r"\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x) dx = 1", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(total_prob, "F3")
        self.play(Write(total_prob))
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Probabilities are integrals over a specific interval.", "Area under the curve equals probability of range.", "Use geometry to find likelihoods of specific zones."]
        self.setup_layout("The Geometric Interpretation", lecture_lines)

        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        label = MathTex(r"P(2 < X < 3)").next_to(area, UP)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: The Squirrel’s Acorn Search", [

            "Curve spikes show where events likely occur.",

        # Elements

        self.place_at_grid(tree, 'A3', scale_factor=0.5)

        # Squirrel icon (placeholder using Square)

        self.place_at_grid(squirrel, 'D1', scale_factor=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#33FF57"), Create(tree), Write(axes))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "PDF is a density, not a probability.",
            "Integration calculates probability from density functions.",
            "Total area must always equal one."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Key Takeaways", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        pdf_def = Text("f(x) = Density", font_size=32)
        prob_int = MathTex(r"\int_{a}^{b} f(x) \,dx = P(a < X < b)", font_size=32)
        total_prob = MathTex(r"\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x) \,dx = 1", font_size=36)
        
        # Axes for PDF illustration
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[0, 1.2, 0.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.exp(-x**2), x_range=[-3, 3])
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[-3, 3], color=BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(pdf_def))
        self.place_at_grid(pdf_def, "B2")
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(prob_int))
        self.place_at_grid(prob_int, "C3")
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF33")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), Create(area))
        self.place_in_area(VGroup(axes, curve, area), "D4", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(total_prob))
        self.place_at_grid(total_prob, "D2")
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: From Discrete to Continuous
sections.content: Briefly recap discrete probability (bars). Transition to continuous variables where the probability of any exact point is zero, shifting the focus from 'height of a bar' to 'area under a curve'.
sections.example: Comparing a histogram of test scores (discrete bars) to a smooth bell curve representing the same data distribution.

sections.title: Defining the PDF
sections.content: Introduce the PDF as a function f(x) where the area under the curve between two points equals the probability. Emphasize two rules: f(x) ≥ 0 and total area = 1.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Probability Fluid' being poured into a container—the total volume (area) must always equal 1 (100% certainty).

sections.title: The Geometric Interpretation
sections.content: Explain that finding the probability of a range [a, b] is equivalent to calculating the integral (area) under the curve between those bounds.
sections.example: A robotic arm's precision: The PDF shows the likelihood of it landing in a specific 2cm zone; we calculate the shaded area to find the success rate.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Squirrel’s Acorn Search
sections.content: Synthesize the knowledge: A squirrel drops an acorn. The PDF shows where it lands. We use the area under the curve to predict the squirrel's most likely hunting zone.
sections.example: An animation showing a squirrel moving across an X-axis; the PDF curve spikes where the squirrel spends most of its time searching.

sections.title: Summary & Key Takeaways
sections.content: Recap: The PDF is not a probability itself, but a density. Integration provides the probability. Total area must equal 1.
sections.example: A 'Cheat Sheet' graphic overlaying a curve with the equation ∫f(x)dx = 1, reinforcing the fundamental rule of total probability.
